relationships.subject: U-II/UT signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: activation of U-II/UT signaling promoted the development of cystitis-associated-bladder hyperactivity by targeting the RhoA/Rho-kinase pathway

key_findings: U-II and UT were upregulated in bladder of cyclophosphamide cystitis rats, including in Cajal-like cells.
UT antagonist SB-657510 reduced bladder hyperactivity, and its effect was abolished by Rho-kinase inhibitor Y-27632, implicating RhoA/ROCK2.
